title: Two AI-found flaws in PHP put much of the web at risk, a hijacked LiteLLM release stole the keys AI teams use, and OpenAI will vet the gateways that resell its models. Anthropic launched the Claude Duet agent app and always-on Claude Security, OpenAI models are coming to Google Cloud, ChatGPT ads reach 89 countries, and Walmart wrote rules for shopping agents.
summary: On 21 October 2026: PHP shipped fixes for two critical flaws, found with frontier AI models, that let attackers run code on web servers without logging in; CISA told organisations to patch immediately. A poisoned LiteLLM 1.107.0 release stole credentials for about two hours, and Railway reported a breach it links to attacks aimed at AI inference providers. OpenAI said that from 20 November model routers and AI gateways need its approval to offer its models, and introduced SafetyIDs. Anthropic opened a waitlist preview of Claude Duet, a proactive agent app that asks before it pays, sends or deletes, and made Claude Security rescan code continuously for Enterprise customers. OpenAI’s models are coming to Google Cloud’s Model Garden, payable from existing Google commitments. ChatGPT ads expanded to 89 countries, and Walmart introduced an agent gateway, per-agent spending limits and terms for AI shopping agents.
uncertainty: Wiz’s ‘70% of websites’ figure is its estimate of PHP’s reach, not a count of vulnerable servers, and CISA had seen no exploitation when it published. LiteLLM’s account of the attack is preliminary, including its finding that Claude Code sometimes embedded GitHub CLI tokens in responses that were later logged; we found no response from Anthropic. Railway has not said how many customers were affected. OpenAI has not yet published the full updated Usage Policies, so it is unclear whether internal company gateways need approval. Claude Duet and the new Claude Security are a preview and a beta, and Anthropic’s usage figures are its own. OpenAI’s advertiser and user numbers, and its statement that ads do not influence answers, are its own. Walmart’s Agent Profiles are not live yet.

stories.theme: Two AI-found flaws in PHP put a large share of the web at risk. Patch now
stories.changed: On Wednesday 21 October 2026 the PHP project released PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 to fix two critical flaws, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, rated 9.2 out of 10. Under the right conditions they let an attacker with no login run code on servers running PHP. Both sit in memory and error handling that nearly every request touches, and on Apache with mod_php one can be triggered before any application code runs. Wiz, which calls the bugs PHP2Shell, says every PHP version of the last decade, back to 5.4, is affected by at least one of them, and it showed attacks without a login on WordPress, Drupal and Joomla, as well as reading passwords and API keys from server memory. Researchers at Calif (working in OpenAI’s Patch the Planet programme), OpenAI and Wiz found the flaws with frontier AI models, including GPT-5.6 Sol and Gemini 4 Argon. The release was brought forward a day after the CVE numbers leaked on 20 October. CISA told organisations to patch immediately and to take systems on PHP 8.1 or older offline until they are updated; it had seen no exploitation when it published.
stories.matters: PHP runs a large share of websites, including WordPress, and is often hidden inside other products. Wiz says frontier models let it build working exploits for a decade-old flaw in hours. Attackers have the same tools, so working attacks may not be far behind.
stories.imply: AI shortens the gap between a fix being published and attacks starting. Patch cycles measured in weeks are no longer safe for internet-facing systems.
uses: Ask IT and every web agency or vendor today which of your sites run PHP and on what version, and update to 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35.
Treat anything on PHP 8.1 or older as urgent: upgrade it, or take it offline as CISA advises.
If you cannot patch at once, switch on your host’s or CDN’s firewall rules for PHP2Shell and watch for PHP processes starting shells.
stories.example: A marketing team finds that a campaign microsite an agency built on WordPress still runs PHP 8.1. The agency takes it offline that afternoon and brings it back on PHP 8.4.27 the next day.
stories.audience: IT and security teams, website owners, web agencies, and any company running WordPress, Drupal or other PHP software.
stories.watch: Reports of attacks in the wild. Fixes from hosts and from products that bundle PHP. Whether more AI-found flaws of this size follow, as OpenAI says it expects.

source.title: The PHP Foundation: Today’s PHP security release, and how we’re strengthening PHP security, 21 October 2026
source.quote: These releases fix two critical vulnerabilities that, under the right conditions, allow an unauthenticated attacker to execute code on servers running PHP.

stories.theme: A hijacked LiteLLM release stole the keys AI teams use to reach their models
stories.changed: On Wednesday 21 October 2026 attackers pushed a malicious version of LiteLLM, a popular open-source gateway that companies use to send requests to many AI providers, through the project’s own release pipeline. Version 1.107.0 was on PyPI from 11:39 to 13:23 UTC, and the Docker images tagged v1.107.0, latest, main-latest and main-stable pointed to the bad build until as late as 14:20 UTC. The malware runs whenever Python starts, steals credentials and can load more code. LiteLLM says the attacker held GitHub CLI tokens belonging to three of its developers, used one owner’s token to override branch protection, and published from a lookalike repository. It believes the tokens came from the logs of an internal LiteLLM deployment exposed to the internet, and says that in some situations Claude Code had embedded a user’s GitHub CLI token in a response that was then logged. The same day, hosting platform Railway said an intruder may have read some customers’ decrypted environment variables, in what it believes is a series of attacks on platform companies aimed at AI inference providers, and GitHub let CLI users opt in to access tokens that stop working within hours.
stories.matters: An AI gateway holds the keys to every model provider a company uses, so one poisoned update can expose all of them at once. Attackers are now going after AI keys and the developer tokens around them.
stories.imply: AI gateways and the machines that run coding agents are high-value targets. Pinned versions, secret-free logs and short-lived tokens are basic hygiene now.
uses: Check whether any machine or container installed litellm 1.107.0 or pulled the latest Docker tags on 21 October. If so, rebuild it and rotate every key it could reach.
Pin LiteLLM and other AI packages to exact versions, and do not deploy a ‘latest’ tag automatically.
Turn on GitHub CLI’s expiring tokens, and stop storing full request and response bodies from coding agents in logs.
stories.example: A platform team finds that a staging LiteLLM container restarted on the latest tag around midday UTC on 21 October. It rebuilds the container on 1.106.2 and rotates its OpenAI, Anthropic and cloud keys the same afternoon.
stories.audience: Engineering, platform and security teams running AI gateways, Python AI tools or coding agents, and Railway customers.
stories.watch: LiteLLM’s final findings on how its internal deployment was reached. Whether Anthropic responds on the Claude Code token issue. More attacks on companies that serve AI models.

source.title: LiteLLM: Oct 21, 2026 LiteLLM release v1.107.0 compromised, 21 October 2026
source.quote: If you ran pip install on LiteLLM v1.107.0 or started the docker image in the compromised interval, assume it is compromised.

stories.theme: From 20 November, AI gateways need OpenAI’s approval to offer its models
stories.changed: On Wednesday 21 October 2026 OpenAI said it is updating its Usage Policies from 20 November 2026. Services that give direct access to its models, such as model routers and AI gateways, will need OpenAI’s review and approval before offering that access. OpenAI says partners that host or resell its models must keep safeguards consistent with its own, investigate possible violations, and coordinate on enforcement so that restrictions stay effective across every service that offers its models. It is also working with customers on SafetyIDs, which customers can send so OpenAI can tell individual end users apart in an investigation without learning who they are, and act on one user with less disruption to others. The announcement came a day after Anthropic let platforms and resellers restrict a single end customer instead of a whole account.
stories.matters: Many companies reach OpenAI models through a router or gateway rather than directly. From 20 November those services need OpenAI’s sign-off, and a restriction is meant to hold across every service that offers its models.
stories.imply: The big labs are tightening control over who resells their models and expect to tell end users apart. Expect fewer unvetted gateways and more requests for user identifiers.
uses: List every router, gateway or reseller your teams use to reach OpenAI models, and ask each whether it has OpenAI’s approval.
If you run an internal AI gateway for staff, ask OpenAI or your account team whether the new rule covers it.
If you build products on OpenAI, plan to send SafetyIDs so one misbehaving user does not get your whole account restricted.
stories.example: A start-up that serves GPT models to its customers through a third-party router asks the router for written confirmation of OpenAI approval before 20 November, and keeps a direct OpenAI key tested as a fallback.
stories.audience: CTOs, platform and procurement teams, and companies building or reselling AI products.
stories.watch: The full text of the updated Usage Policies. Which gateways are approved. Whether internal company gateways count. Whether Google follows.

source.title: OpenAI: Broad access through consistent standards, 21 October 2026
source.quote: The updated Usage Policies build on that work by requiring services that provide direct access to our models such as model routers or AI gateways to get our review and approval before offering that access.

stories.theme: Anthropic’s Claude Duet watches your work apps and acts, but asks first
stories.changed: On Wednesday 21 October 2026 Anthropic opened a research preview of Claude Duet, a separate app on iOS, Android and claude.ai in which Claude works as a proactive agent. Access is by waitlist, starting with Pro and Max subscribers in the US, and it shares the plan’s usage limits with the rest of Claude. Built around Claude Opus 5.5, it sends a short morning brief on the most important items across your connected apps, checks those apps every few hours and messages you when something needs you, and works on tasks in the background in its own virtual machine with a browser, so your laptop can be off. It carries over your Claude memory, skills and connected apps, and can use the more than 6,000 connectors and plugins in the Claude Marketplace, from Gmail and Slack to QuickBooks, Stripe, Gusto and Docusign. Before it sends a message, makes a payment, signs a document or deletes anything, it shows exactly what it will do and waits for approval; trading securities and moving money between accounts are off-limits even with approval. A new classifier rejects requests to share card numbers and government ID. Anthropic says it may misread a thread or misjudge what is urgent, and that its background checks count against your limits.
stories.matters: Assistants are moving from answering when asked to watching your inbox and accounts and acting on them. The approval step is the main safeguard, so it only works if the person approving actually reads what they approve.
stories.imply: Agents with standing access to email, calendars and finance tools are arriving for professionals and small businesses. Companies will need rules on which work accounts may be connected to them.
uses: If you join the preview, connect one or two work apps first and judge the morning brief for a week before connecting finance tools.
Decide which actions always need a person’s approval, such as payments, payroll and contracts, and never approve them without reading.
IT teams: decide whether staff may connect company email and Slack to a personal Pro or Max plan.
stories.example: A small-agency owner asks Duet to check Stripe for unpaid invoices every Friday and draft reminders. She reads each draft before approving it, and keeps payroll off its list.
stories.audience: Small-business owners, consultants and managers on Claude Pro or Max in the US, and IT teams setting AI rules.
stories.watch: When it reaches other countries and Team or Enterprise plans. How much of a plan’s limits the background checks use. How well its judgement about what is urgent holds up.

source.title: Claude by Anthropic: Introducing Claude Duet, 21 October 2026
source.quote: before it sends a message, makes a payment, signs a document, or deletes anything, it shows you exactly what it’s about to do and waits for your approval.

stories.theme: Claude Security now rescans your code as it changes and tracks fixes
stories.changed: On Wednesday 21 October 2026 Anthropic released a new version of Claude Security, its AI code-vulnerability scanner, in public beta for Claude Enterprise customers. Instead of one-off scans, it runs a deep baseline scan of connected repositories, through the Claude GitHub app (including GitHub Enterprise Server) or an access token for GitLab and other Git providers, then rescans changes based on their risk and complexity. It marks findings fixed when the fix lands, wherever the fix was made, and reopens them if the issue comes back. Each project has a knowledge base where teams describe how code is deployed and which controls apply, plus an editable threat model generated from the code that sets each finding’s severity, and findings explain how an attacker could reach the code. A new API with webhooks, an MCP connector for Claude Code, and role-based access controls are included. Anthropic says thousands of organisations have used it to find more than a million vulnerabilities since April, and is giving organisations $25,000 of free usage a month for two months, for usage up to 31 December 2026.
stories.matters: On the day AI-found PHP flaws hit much of the web, a scanner that keeps pace with every change matters more. Fix tracking turns a one-off audit into a shared, running list for security and engineering.
stories.imply: AI code scanning is becoming part of the normal development pipeline, not an annual exercise. The context and threat model you give it will decide how useful its findings are.
uses: If you are on Claude Enterprise, use the free credits to scan one critical service and compare the findings with your current scanner.
Fill in the knowledge base properly: how code is deployed, which controls exist and what outsiders can reach.
Send new findings to your ticket system through webhooks so each one gets an owner.
stories.example: A fintech security team connects its payments repositories, records its API gateway’s checks in the knowledge base, and routes new high-severity findings to the owning team’s queue.
stories.audience: Security and engineering leads at companies on Claude Enterprise.
stories.watch: Pricing after the free credits. How many findings turn out to be false alarms. How it compares with the AI scanners from GitHub and OpenAI.

source.title: Claude by Anthropic: Claude Security now scans continuously and tracks fixes, 21 October 2026
source.quote: Claude Security checks open findings against the code that changed and marks them fixed when the fix lands, whether your team fixed it in Claude Code or in a separate process.

stories.theme: OpenAI’s models are coming to Google Cloud, paid from existing commitments
stories.changed: On Wednesday 21 October 2026 OpenAI and Google Cloud said OpenAI’s frontier models and Codex agentic workflows are coming to Model Garden, Google Cloud’s catalogue of AI models. Customers will buy them through the Google Cloud Marketplace, and companies with Google Cloud spending commitments will be able to count these purchases against them. OpenAI models will also come to Google Antigravity, Google’s coding tool, and the Gemini Agent. General availability is planned in the coming weeks, with access by request until then. OpenAI says Microsoft remains its primary cloud partner.
stories.matters: For companies standardised on Google Cloud, using GPT models no longer means a separate contract and bill. Money already committed to Google can pay for it, and governance stays in one place.
stories.imply: Frontier models are becoming available on every major cloud, so the choice of model is separating from the choice of cloud. That gives buyers more room to negotiate.
uses: If you have a Google Cloud commitment, ask your account team how OpenAI usage will count against it and how its price compares with buying from OpenAI directly.
Request preview access and run the same tasks on GPT and Gemini models side by side.
Check whether your Google Cloud security and data-residency reviews cover OpenAI models served there.
stories.example: A retailer with a large Google Cloud commitment plans to move an email-drafting workload from a separate OpenAI contract to Model Garden once it is generally available, paying from its existing commitment.
stories.audience: CTOs, cloud, finance and procurement teams at companies on Google Cloud.
stories.watch: Prices, models and regions at general availability. When GPT arrives in Antigravity and the Gemini Agent.

source.title: OpenAI: OpenAI models are coming to Google Cloud, 21 October 2026
source.quote: Enterprises with Google Cloud spend commitments will be able to draw down their GCP commitments for these purchases.

stories.theme: ChatGPT ads now run in 89 countries, with more than 100,000 advertisers
stories.changed: On Wednesday 21 October 2026 OpenAI expanded ChatGPT ads to 26 more countries, bringing them to 89. The new markets include 14 more Latin American countries, among them Argentina, Chile, Colombia and Peru, as well as countries such as Nigeria, South Africa, Serbia, Ukraine, Cambodia, Bangladesh and Pakistan. OpenAI says more than 100,000 advertisers have run campaigns in the eight months since ads launched, and that more than 1.2 billion people use ChatGPT each week. Ads appear only on the Free and Go plans; Plus, Pro and Enterprise stay ad-free. Advertisers can buy through technology partners or self-serve through Ads Manager. OpenAI says conversations are kept private from advertisers, ads are labelled and kept separate from answers, and advertising does not influence what ChatGPT says. Next it plans more ad formats, objectives, buying options and measurement.
stories.matters: ChatGPT is becoming an ad channel in many more markets, reaching people while they compare options and decide what to buy. For marketers it is a new place to appear; staff using free accounts for work will see ads next to their answers.
stories.imply: AI assistants are turning into a marketing channel, much as search did. Expect growing pressure on brands to show up in AI answers, paid and unpaid.
uses: Marketing teams in the new countries: run a small test campaign through Ads Manager and compare cost per lead with search ads.
Check how your brand and competitors appear in ChatGPT answers to the questions customers ask before buying.
If staff use free ChatGPT accounts for work, remind them that ads are not advice, or move them to a paid business plan.
stories.example: An online furniture shop in Colombia runs a two-week test of ChatGPT ads around conversations about furnishing a new flat, and compares the cost per order with its search ads.
stories.audience: Marketing and growth teams, especially in Latin America, Africa, Eastern Europe and South Asia, and managers choosing ChatGPT plans.
stories.watch: New ad formats and measurement tools. Independent checks that ads do not affect answers. Which countries come next.

source.title: OpenAI: ChatGPT Ads expands to 26 new countries as over 100,000 advertisers have used the platform, 21 October 2026
source.quote: Ads will appear only on the Free and Go plans.

stories.theme: Walmart gives shopping agents their own profiles, spending limits and rules
stories.changed: On Wednesday 21 October 2026 Walmart introduced tools and terms for AI agents that shop for customers at Walmart and Sam’s Club. The Walmart Agent Gateway, an MCP server starting as a beta for companies and developers, lets approved agents search inventory and buy for a user, and can help an agent find a customer’s usual items without sharing their wider purchase history. Agent Profiles, arriving within the next month, give each agent its own profile inside the customer’s account, so its purchases show separately, with either approval for every purchase or a spending limit the customer sets, such as $50, $100 or $200. Walmart’s terms say agents may not go beyond what the shopper intends, never receive payment-card details, may use only the information the task needs, and will be blocked if they break the rules. Purchases need approval by default, and Walmart’s returns process applies even when an agent does not act as intended. Chief executive John Furner announced it at the Masters of Scale Summit, shortly after Amazon began blocking AI agents from buying for shoppers.
stories.matters: Big retailers are splitting on agents: Amazon blocks them, Walmart writes rules for them. Separate profiles, spending caps and returns for agent mistakes are a template for any business that lets agents act on customer accounts.
stories.imply: Agents are getting their own identities, limits and terms of use, much like an extra cardholder. Other retailers and suppliers will have to choose between blocking agents and opening a gateway.
uses: E-commerce teams: decide whether to block, tolerate or welcome AI shopping agents, and write down the terms they must follow.
If you let an agent buy for your business, give it its own profile or account and a spending limit.
Check how your returns and disputes process handles purchases an agent made by mistake.
stories.example: A café owner links a shopping agent to her Walmart account with a $100 limit for weekly supplies. Anything above the limit waits for her approval, and the agent’s orders appear separately from her own.
stories.audience: E-commerce, retail and payments teams, and small businesses that use agents for purchasing.
stories.watch: When Agent Profiles launch and which agents are approved. Whether Amazon and other retailers change course.

source.title: TechCrunch: While Amazon blocks AI agents, Walmart rolls out the welcome mat, 21 October 2026
source.quote: Of note, Walmart says that its returns process applies, including when an agent doesn’t act as intended.
